This appeal coming on for admission this day, the court passed the following:
 ORDER Assailing the award dated 23/4/2010 passed by the Ninth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Fast Track), Gwalior in Claim Case No.249/2009, on the point o f inadequacy of the compensation, the appellants have preferred this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sentences.text: The appellants had filed the claim petition under Sections 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs.15,74,000/- on account of death of deceased Sonam Qureshi (daughter of appellants) in an accident took place on 25/9/2005.

3. The reply to the claim petition was filed and after recording the evidence, the Tribunal has awarded the total sum of Rs. 1,80,000/-, out of which in loss of dependency Rs.1,50,000/- accepting the notional annual earning of the deceased Rs. 15,000/-, applying the multiplier of 15.
The Tribunal has also awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- under conventional heads like funeral expenses and loss of estate by the impugned award.

4. As the incident occurred, negligence of driver of driving the offending vehicle, the issue of liability jointly and severally to pay compensation have been decided recording the findings in favour of the appellants by the Tribunal and none of those findings have been assailed at the instance of the respondents i.e. owner, driver or insurance company by filing the cross-appeal or the cross-objection, however it is not necessary to narrate the entire facts in detail to burden the judgment on the said issues.

It is only the inadequacy of the compensation which has been assailed,
however the arguments in detail have been considered in succeeding paragraphs.
5.

Shri Goyal, learned counsel representing the appellants contends that due to the said accident Ku.
Sonam has died.
The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate, because the earning has not been duly assessed while determining the loss of dependency.
The amount awarded under the conventional heads is also on lower side.
No amount has been awarded under the head future prospects.
In view of the foregoing submissions, the enhancement of the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal has been prayed for.

6. On the other hand Shri Sharma, learned counsel representing the respondent /Insurance Company contends in support of the findings of the Claims Tribunal and submitted that the compensation as awarded by the impugned award appears to be just a n d reasonable, however,
interference by this Court for enhancement of the compensation is not warranted.
7.

After having heard learned counsel appearing for the parties and on perusal of the pleadings and the evidence so adduced, it appears that the monthly income of deceased as assessed by the Claim Tribunal is on lower side.
No amount has been awarded under the heads future prospects.

Thus after hearing and on due deliberations and also on consideration of the totality of the facts and circumstances, in the opinion of this Court, the amount of compensation as awarded by the Claims Tribunal is liable to be enhanced by Rs. 1,10,000/- in lump sum thereby making the total compensation Rs. 2,90,000/- which shall be payable along with the interest from the date of filing of the claim petition.
8. In view of the forgoing discussions, the appeal succeeds and is hereby allowed in part.
The appellants are held entitled to receive the enhanced amount of Rs. 1,102,000/- in addition to the amount of compensation already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by Claims Tribunal shall remain intact.

In the facts of the case, parties are Hakimuddin Kureshi vs Vivek Rathore on 13 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110039437/
